brief.headline: Nifty Gains 1.74% as Oil Drops; US Tariffs Threaten Tech Rally
brief.summary: Indian equities surged with Nifty reaching 25791.25 and Bank Nifty gaining 1.70%, aided by a drop in Brent crude to $88.49. However, weak global cues, tech sell-offs in US markets, and potential US tariff hikes on India and China present overnight headwinds.

takeaways.text: ICICI Bank hit record highs as JPMorgan named it top pick, with all 52 covering analysts maintaining buy ratings after an 18% November gain.
APL Apollo Tubes locked in a 15% lower circuit post acquiring Tata Steel units for ₹28,000-crore, while Tata Steel bought a 9.91% stake for ₹5,825 crore.
Crude-linked stocks including IndiGo, BPCL, and Asian Paints surged up to 4% as Brent crude prices eased to $88.
US markets dropped with the Nasdaq down 1.48% and S&P 500 down 0.50% as tech shares faced selling pressure and tariff concerns mounted.
Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addressed staff following his reinstatement.

sections.india: Indian benchmark indices posted strong gains, with Nifty rising 1.74% to 25791.25 and Sensex up 1.77% to 83896.59. Bank Nifty advanced 1.70% to 63651.55 led by heavyweight private banks. APL Apollo Tubes crashed 15% following its ₹28,000-crore acquisition announcement of Tata Steel businesses, while L&T gained over 2% on winning a ₹2,500 crore battery storage project in Gujarat. Softening crude prices provided relief to paints, aviation, and OMC shares.
sections.world: US markets closed lower overnight as Nasdaq fell 1.48% and S&P 500 slipped 0.50%, despite the Dow Jones gaining 0.85%. Concerns over potential fresh US tariff hikes targeting India, China, and 15 other economies over industrial subsidies weighed on market sentiment. Gold prices declined near $3,500 a troy ounce as investors awaited US inflation data, while Asian markets opened mixed with Nikkei 225 dropping 2.78%.
sections.tech: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during an all-hands meeting after his return, denying reports regarding White House involvement. Anthropic shares tumbled below their $83 IPO price, putting pressure on tech valuations. Meanwhile, McKinsey research revealed only 6 per cent of surveyed banks have realized substantial financial returns from AI productivity gains, and Foxconn's India unit faced an insolvency plea over ₹143 Cr in alleged dues.
